fear.name: Despair
fear.hint: The Despair pool of the GM.

forcePrivateRolls.name: Force private player rolls
forcePrivateRolls.hint: Every player roll is whispered to that player and the GMs. Nobody sees anyone else's dice.

enforceAnonymity.name: Keep character sheets anonymous
enforceAnonymity.hint: Holds default ownership at None, so no player can open another player's sheet. Each player still owns their own.

searchTokensPerRoom.name: Search tokens per room
searchTokensPerRoom.hint: How many times one room can be searched in a single time of day.

lockRollDialog.name: Lock the roll window for players
lockRollDialog.hint: Players cannot touch the dice, the statistic, advantage, experiences or the bonus — those come from the action, a Hope Call or the GM. Spending an experience is the Experience Hope Call. GMs are unaffected.

roomVisibility.name: Players only see who is in their room
roomVisibility.hint: Hides other characters unless they stand in the same room. Walls and vision get most of the way there; this closes the gaps left by doorways, archways and maps built without walls. GMs see everything.

isoTokenShield.name: Guard token editing from Isometric Perspective
isoTokenShield.hint: While the isometric-perspective module is active, its additions to token configuration windows are kept out — they are what breaks token editing on some setups. The map's projection is untouched, and so is the Scene configuration. Turn this off to reach that module's own Isometric tab on tokens; it comes back immediately, no reload.

regionFog.name: Rooms decide what players can see
regionFog.hint: Lights the whole map and lets the module's room fog do the hiding: the room you are in is clear, rooms you have been to show through a veil, the rest is fogged. Off, Foundry's own line-of-sight vision applies. GMs see everything.

lockPlayerResources.name: Players cannot edit Actions, Hope or statistics
lockPlayerResources.hint: Those move through play — spend an action, take a rest, earn a Level Up. Health and Sanity stay editable: players mark their own damage. GMs are unaffected.

chargeMovement.name: Crossing rooms costs a Move
chargeMovement.hint: Moving inside a room is free. Crossing into another Scene Region spends the free Move for that time of day, then an action. Turn off to handle movement by hand.

despairFromRolls.name: Rolls grant Despair
despairFromRolls.hint: A roll that lands with Despair feeds the pool of that student's Monokuma. Divide the students up from the gear on the Despair bar.

hideSystemFear.name: Replace the Daggerheart Fear tracker
hideSystemFear.hint: Hides Daggerheart's single shared Fear bar and gives every Monokuma a Despair pool of their own. Turn off to go back to the system tracker.

pixelFont.name: Pixel font
pixelFont.hint: Press Start 2P on interface chrome: HUD, Despair, character name, statistic labels, tabs. Journals, chat and editable fields keep the normal face so long text stays readable.

debug.name: Verbose console logging
debug.hint: Print Danganronpa RPG diagnostics to the browser console. This client only.

musicEnabled.name: Music follows the game state
musicEnabled.hint: Swaps the playlist when the Eclipse opens, a Class Trial or Investigation begins, the time of day turns, or the game goes on hold. Map the playlists first: GM panel → Right now → Music by state. A murder incident never changes the music.

voiceEnabled.name: Regional voice (needs LiveKit AVClient)
voiceEnabled.hint: Every mapped room becomes its own LiveKit channel — you hear only whoever stands in the room with you. Needs avclient-livekit installed, active and pointed at a working server. Off by default.

Action.observeGm: Total {total}. Score it against the Observe table for whatever they are looking at. A failure costs them 2 Sanity.
Action.searchGoalHint: What turns up depends on the room and the roll.
Action.goalCrimeHint: A potential murder tool. Leaves a Prep Remnant.
Action.goalCleaningHint: A cleaning tool. Leaves a Prep Remnant.
Action.goalSpecificHint: Describe it. The GM rules on what was really there.
Action.goalSpecificPlaceholder: e.g. anything belonging to the victim
Action.goalSpecificNeeded: Describe what you are looking for first.
Action.specificFound: The roll reached Tier {tier}. Decide what was there.

Action.specificSent: Your description is with the GM. They will say what you found.
Action.dynamicHint: Describe what you are doing; the GM sets the difficulty. Dynamic actions have gentler thresholds than the standard ones — that is the reward for inventing something.
Action.dynamicDescribe: Describe what your character does. The GM reads this and sets the difficulty.
Action.dynamicPlaceholder: e.g. I water the plants in the garden, looking for anything buried.
Action.dynamicNoRuling: No GM answered. The attempt is off and nothing was spent.
Action.dynamicDescription: Any action at all, provided you describe it in detail — the GM sets the difficulty and the statistic. The thresholds are gentler than the standard actions, as a deliberate reward for inventing something.
Action.noRoomNote: Your token is outside every room.
Action.callsGmNote: The GM judges this one. Your roll and your request go to them.
Action.gmPrompt: {action} — what are you trying to do? The GM sees this with your roll.

placeholder.directMurder: Who, where and how — as agreed beforehand.

Action.analyzeGm: Score this against the Analyze table for that Truth Bullet. A failure locks it for them until the chapter ends.
Action.murderConfirm: This opens a direct murder. It needs prior agreement with the GM and the consent of the other player. The action is spent even if the conditions fail.
Action.murderNobody: Nobody here to kill. The attempt is spent; try again another time of day.

murderWitness.one: You are not alone with your victim — {n} other person would see it. The attempt is spent; try again another time of day.
murderWitness.other: You are not alone with your victim — {n} other people would see it. The attempt is spent; try again another time of day.

Action.sabotageSeen: {actor} is seen doing something to a project in {room}.
Action.sabotageWatched: {actor} is doing something to {project} in {room}, and everyone here can see roughly what.
Action.sabotageCarryOn: Carry on anyway? Nothing is spent yet.
Action.murderSpendsAnyway: Confirming spends the action whether or not it comes off — and you will not find out which until the Eclipse ends.
Action.murderPromptParked: What are you doing, and how? The GM reads this when the lights come up.
Action.murderParked: Your move is made. The GM has to allow it, and nobody knows how it went — not even you — until the Eclipse ends and the room settles.
Action.murderParkedToast: Declared. The answer comes when the Eclipse does.
Action.murderAlreadyRunning: Somebody else got there first. An incident was already running when the lights came up, and the action is spent.
Action.murderSecondDeclaration: {killer} also declared a direct murder in the dark, but an incident was already open. Their attempt was refused and their action is spent.
Action.murderCancelled: {killer}'s direct murder came to nothing in {room} — {reason}
Action.murderOpens: {killer} declared a direct murder during the Eclipse and ended it alone with {victim} in {room}. The incident is open.
Action.noVariants: Nothing here can be done right now.
Action.requestOptional: Optional — leave it empty and the GM rules on the roll alone.
Action.murderNeedsApproval: A direct murder, declared in the dark. Nothing opens until you allow it — and who they end up alone with is not settled yet.
Action.murderApproved: The GM has allowed the attempt. What comes of it still depends on where everyone ends up.
Action.murderRefused: The GM did not allow it. The action is spent.
Action.murderApprovedGm: {name}'s direct murder is allowed. It resolves when the Eclipse ends.
Action.murderRefusedGm: {name}'s direct murder is refused. Their action is spent.
Action.murderNotParked: That declaration is no longer waiting — the Eclipse has ended, or it has already been ruled on.
Action.murderAsk: {killer} declared a direct murder in the dark and has ended up alone with {victim} in {room}. Open the incident?
Action.murderAskNote: You were asked this when it was declared and it is still unanswered. Refusing opens nothing; the action stays spent either way.

analyseBulletHint.other: Work out what one of your {n} unidentified Truth Bullets really is.

Monocub.opted: {name} has joined the GMs as a Monocub.
Monocub.dialogIntro: A dead player may join the GMs as a Monocub once their own trial has ended. Tick to opt them in — the timing is your judgement, not the module's.
Monocub.giveHope: Turn a Monokuma's Despair into Hope
Monocub.silencedNote: Tick if this Monocub stumbled onto the crime scene. They cannot discuss it until the chapter ends, but Confusion still works on the incident's crisis actions.
Monocub.needHope: Confusion costs Hope and you have none. Ask a GM to convert some Despair.
Monocub.nobodyHere: Nobody in this room to use Confusion on.
Monocub.meddleIntro: Nudge somebody's next roll from the sidelines. They will not know it was you.
Monocub.silencedNoteShort: You stumbled onto the crime. No discussing it until next chapter.
Monocub.noneYet: Nobody has opted in as a Monocub yet.
Monocub.silenceOn: You stumbled onto the crime. You may not discuss it until this chapter ends.
Monocub.silenceOff: The silence is lifted. You may discuss the crime again.
Monocub.silencedTooltip: A Monokuma has taken your voice for the rest of the chapter. You may act, but you may not speak at the table.

Mastermind.lairNote: From inside this room they see every token on the map, the way you do; step out and it is gone. Locked doors, seals, other bedrooms and hidden stashes already open for them everywhere — the room is where the cameras are.
Mastermind.finalRunningNote: This trial is the Final Trial.
Mastermind.privacyWarning: This screen names the Mastermind. Do not share your view while it is open.
Mastermind.dialogIntro: Picked before the season, with the player's agreement. Despair converts into their Hope 1:1 — the same trade a Monocub gets.
Mastermind.noneSet: No Mastermind set. Pick one from the GM panel first.
Mastermind.toggleFinalTrial: Start or end the Final Trial
Mastermind.confirmStart: Announce the Final Trial? This is public — everyone sees it start.
Mastermind.confirmEnd: Clear the Final Trial flag? Nothing already applied is undone.
Mastermind.ended: The Final Trial flag is cleared.
Mastermind.finalTruthPlaced: A Final Truth Remnant has already been placed this chapter.
Mastermind.finalTruthReminder: No Final Truth Remnant this chapter yet. One a chapter, pointing at the Mastermind — drop it with the ordinary Remnant tools, type “Final Truth Remnant”.
Mastermind.verdictIntro: Only you know whether the vote named the Mastermind. Say who was accused and pick the outcome.
Mastermind.alreadyDeadNote: The Mastermind died earlier this season. The same rule applies whoever was accused: reveal the truth, execute nobody new.
Mastermind.verdictNote: Correct: the Mastermind is executed and the killing game is over. Wrong, or already dead: nobody new is executed — the table is shown that the game was never what it looked like.
Mastermind.revealedText: The game they were playing was never what it seemed.
Mastermind.confirmed: {name} is the Mastermind. Only the GMs know, and nothing was written to the world.
Mastermind.cleared: The Mastermind is cleared. Nobody is set.
Mastermind.finalAnnounce: This is the last one. Everything you have been told about this place is on the table, and so is whoever has been telling it to you.
Mastermind.finalRemnantsNote: The clues the endgame turns on. Their type reinforces them, so nobody can clean one away.
Mastermind.finalAddNote: Leave the room empty to change nothing. The clue is placed on the scene you are looking at, somewhere inside the room.

Floor.nobody: There is nobody alive to open the debate with.
Floor.startTrialIntro: A Class Trial opens in discussion: everybody talks, and evidence goes on the table without taking the floor. The Nonstop Debate is something you open inside it.
Floor.startTrialStepPhase: The campaign moves to Class Trial.
Floor.startTrialStepAnnounce: The trial is announced in chat and the music follows.
Floor.trialOpened: The Class Trial is in session. Talk it through; the debate opens when the GM says so.
Floor.endTrialConfirm: This closes the debate, ends the Class Trial and returns the campaign to Daily Life.
Floor.objectionNote: You never move the debate for an objection: presenting evidence takes it.
Floor.manageRunning: A Class Trial is running. Open the debate when the room is ready to argue, and work down the sections below: the vote, the verdict, then the end of the chapter.
Floor.manageNotRunning: No Class Trial is running. Starting one sets the phase and announces it to the table — the trial opens in discussion, and you open the debate inside it.
Floor.discussionNote: The debate's clock is your budget for it, not a limit: running past it turns the clock red and nothing else. An OBJECTION is what takes the debate away from the table.
Floor.holdingDiscussion: Open discussion — {seconds} s left on your budget. Everyone may speak.
Floor.holdingObjection: {who} holds the debate, objecting to {target} — {seconds} s. Nobody else may speak; the rebuttal follows automatically.
Floor.holdingRebuttal: Rebuttal: {who} and {target}, {seconds} s. Only those two; it returns to open discussion by itself.
Floor.modeNote: This runs out on its own. Use the buttons below to cut it short, give it another half minute, or drop straight back to the open debate.
Floor.noDebate: No Class Trial is running, so there is no debate to hold.
Floor.sectionVote: The vote, the verdict, the chapter
Floor.debateOpened: The Nonstop Debate is open. Presenting a Truth Bullet is now an OBJECTION: it takes the floor.
Floor.debateClosed: The debate is closed. The trial carries on as an open discussion.
Floor.inDiscussion: The trial is in open discussion — everybody may talk, and evidence goes on the table without taking the floor.
Floor.trialClosed: The Class Trial is over. Daily Life resumes.
Floor.startTrialStepDiscussion: The trial opens in discussion. You open the debate when you want one.
Floor.gateVote: The verdict opens once the vote has been counted.
Floor.gateVerdict: The vote is counted. Deliver the verdict, then end the chapter.
Floor.gateDone: The verdict is in. The chapter can end.
Floor.startTrialNote: The clock starts over: the campaign's elapsed timer restarts with the trial, and again when it ends.
Floor.openDebateIntro: How long is this debate worth? Each one in a trial gets its own budget, and the last number you used is offered.

Vote.openIntro: Send every player a ballot, then count them. Both halves are this button.
Vote.privacyNote: Ballots never touch world data. They go to the GMs, are counted in memory and are not kept. The results are published; the votes are not.
Vote.opened: {n} ballots are out. Name who you believe is the Blackened.
Vote.noVoters: No player is connected with a character to vote.
Vote.ballotIntro: Vote for whoever you believe is the Blackened. You may vote for yourself, for Monokuma, and for the dead.
Vote.ballotNote: Nobody sees who you voted for. Only the totals are published.
Vote.dismissed: Ballot closed without a vote. Nothing was counted for you — ask the GM to send it again.
Vote.notRunning: No vote is open right now.
Vote.tied: A tie. That is a loss for the students.
Vote.verdictIntro: Only you know whether they got it right. Name who is executed and who the Blackened really was, then pick the outcome.
Vote.verdictNote: Right: the Blackened is executed and every survivor takes a Level Up. Wrong — a tie counts as wrong — the accused is executed, the Blackened stays in play with a Reinforced Level Up and a new rule, and every Monokuma fills their Despair.
Vote.wrongSummary: The students named the wrong person.

blackenedRewarded.one: The Blackened stays anonymous and in play, and takes a {kind} Level Up.
blackenedRewarded.other: {n} Blackened stay anonymous and in play, and each takes a {kind} Level Up.

Vote.newRule: The Blackened introduces one new rule of their choosing, with Monokuma's consent.
Vote.twoBlackened: This chapter produced {n} Blackened. Name all of them — half an answer is not one.

silent.one: 1 ballot never came back. The count above is out of every ballot issued.
silent.other: {n} ballots never came back. The count above is out of every ballot issued.

Vote.executedIfWrong: Executed instead, if the table got it wrong
Vote.verdictNoteKnown: Getting it right executes the Blackened above — you do not have to name anybody. Getting it wrong executes whoever the table accused, and every killer walks away with a Reinforced Level Up. A tie counts as wrong.
Vote.verdictIntroKnown: Only you know whether they got it right. The module remembers who killed — all you have to say is whether the table found them.

Music.title: Music
Music.intro: Pick which playlist plays when. The module never starts a playlist you have not chosen here, and ships no audio of its own.
Music.orderNote: The first state that applies wins, in the order listed. A Class Trial at night uses the trial's playlist; an Eclipse during one uses the Eclipse's.
Music.incidentNote: A murder incident has no entry on purpose. A track that only ever played during one would tell the whole table a murder is happening. Whatever is playing keeps playing.
Music.fadeNote: Fades are the playlist's own — set Fade Duration on the playlist or on a track, and both directions use it. Put a track on and everything else pauses where it stands, then resumes from there.
Music.noPlaylists: This world has no playlists, so there is nothing to map to yet. Make them in the Playlists sidebar; the cue playlist on the Play tab can be made from here.
Music.playNowNote: Plays one track from the “{name}” playlist on repeat. Whatever is playing pauses where it stands and comes back when you reset.
Music.wasReset: The track is off and whatever it interrupted is back where it left off.
Music.playFailed: That track would not play. See the console.
Music.noSituational: This world has no playlist called “{name}”. The button below makes it with exactly that name — the module finds it by name, so a near miss is a playlist it will quietly ignore.
Music.situationalMade: “{name}” exists now. Put your scene tracks in it from the Playlists sidebar — stings, reveals, the quiet bits — and they will appear here.
Music.makeFailed: The playlist could not be created. See the console.

Cleanup.title: Cleaning up
Cleanup.hint: Spend 1 Sanity to erase one trace you left. A readied Cleaning Tool makes it easier. Reinforced traces do not come off.
Cleanup.intro: Wiping a trace costs an action and {n} Sanity, and you have two actions this time of day.
Cleanup.withTool: {item} (Tier {tier}) in hand — advantage, and that much off the threshold.
Cleanup.noneReadied: No Cleaning Tool readied. Hold one ready on the Inventory tab first.

blocked.noIncident: No incident is running, so there is nothing to clean up. Stage 6 opens when one ends.
blocked.notYet: The incident is still going on. Clean-up opens the moment it is over — as a Finishing Blow, or by the GM ending it.
blocked.notYours: You are not the one cleaning up this scene.
blocked.monokuma: Monokuma does not clean up after himself. A killing made as a point is meant to be found.

Cleanup.trailHint: Spend 1 Sanity to plant a trace pointing at somebody else. A failure still plants something — just a Faint one nobody is likely to find.
Cleanup.trailIntro: Planting a false trail costs an action and {n} Sanity.
Cleanup.trailNobody: There is nobody left to frame.
Cleanup.moveHint: Spend 1 Sanity to carry the body out of this room. It always leaves an Evident trace — a body cannot be dragged quietly.
Cleanup.bodyNotHere: The body is not in this room. You have to be standing over it to carry it anywhere.
Cleanup.nothingHere: Nothing to clean up in this room.
Cleanup.allReinforced: Every trace here is reinforced. None of it comes off.
Cleanup.noRuling: No GM answered in time. Try again once one is at the table.
Cleanup.rerollLost: A Reroll arrived for a clean-up with no record here. Score the new number against that trace by hand, then put the Remnant back or refund the Sanity to match.
Cleanup.reinforced: The {what} will not come off. Whatever left it, left it for good.
Cleanup.vanished: The trace you were working on is already gone. The effort still cost you.
Cleanup.leftTrace: Your cleaning left a trace of its own.

band.despair: Gone — but you were not careful about it.
band.failure: It will not come off, and you made a mess trying.

Cleanup.gmTool: Readied: {item} (Tier {tier}) — advantage, and {tier} off every threshold below.
Cleanup.gmNoTool: No Cleaning Tool readied — bare hands, no advantage.
Cleanup.gmNothingHere: No traces in the room the killer is standing in.

gmAttemptsLeft.one: Sanity left for {n} more attempt. Stage 6 ends when that runs out, or when you close the murder — closing destroys the tools that were used.
gmAttemptsLeft.other: Sanity left for {n} more attempts. Stage 6 ends when that runs out, or when you close the murder — closing destroys the tools that were used.

Cleanup.trailPlanted: Planted a Prep Remnant ({visibility}) pointing at {name}.
Cleanup.bodyMoved: The body has been moved to {room}.
Cleanup.bodyStuck: There is nowhere to take it.
Cleanup.noBody: There is no body here to move.
Cleanup.bodyNote: {name}'s body was dragged out of here towards {room}.
Cleanup.seenCleaning: {actor} is doing something in {room}, and not hiding it well.
Cleanup.moveIntro: The body is in {room}. Choose where you are dragging it. Costs an action and {n} Sanity.
Cleanup.moveAlwaysTrace: This always leaves an Evident trace behind, whatever the dice say. You cannot drag a corpse quietly.
Cleanup.bodyNowhere: There is nowhere to take it — no room connects to this one.
Cleanup.toolsBroken: {items} is ruined. It is still in your inventory, and it is still evidence.

Murder.openIntro: One opening roll, then a turn-based incident. A direct murder opens on the killer's roll; a trap opens on the victim's.
Murder.indirect: Indirect murder — the victim is alone, and the drain is doubled
Murder.needOne: There must be at least one living student.
Murder.openSelfNote: One name in both seats: this opens as a death by their own hand. There is no Stage 5 — the opening roll decides whether they go through with it and how many Key Remnants the scene keeps, and the incident goes straight to Stage 6.
Murder.opened: {killer} is moving on {victim}. The opening roll has gone to {roller}.
Murder.openedSelf: {name} is moving on themselves. The opening roll has gone to them.
Murder.openedSelfNote: Stage 5 is skipped: there is no confrontation to run. If the roll lands, the incident goes straight to Stage 6 — the arrangements they make before dying. They stay alive until you close the incident, which is what records the death.
Murder.selfWentThrough: You went through with it. There is no fight to have. Stage 6 is open on your sheet: whatever you leave the room as, you leave it as now.
Murder.resolutionNoteSelf: Stage 6, with nobody left to hide it from but the class. They can see and clean their own traces, and they are still alive to do it — closing the incident is what makes the death real.
Murder.trackerStateSelf: {stage} · no turns — Stage 5 does not run
Murder.afterSelf: By their own hand — nobody else was in the room, and the class has only the scene to go on.
Murder.afterIntroSelf: {name}, by their own hand. Everything below follows from what just happened, and the module has stopped tracking the incident itself.
Murder.dayNote: Not night, so the opening roll is unmodified.
Murder.keyCount: This case will leave {n} Key Remnants.
Murder.ranOut: {name} is out of Health and out of Sanity. The incident ends and they are dead — no Finishing Blow was needed, and none was earned.
Murder.rerollLost: A Reroll arrived for a crisis action with no record here. Nothing was replayed, so the first result stands. Score the new number by hand.
Murder.nobodyElse: There is nobody else alive to walk in.
Murder.endConfirm: Close this murder? The incident state is cleared. Nothing already applied is undone.
Murder.afterTitle: The incident is over — what now
Murder.afterIntro: {killer} against {victim}. Everything below follows from what just happened, and the module has stopped tracking the incident itself.
Murder.afterNoRoom: The victim's token is outside every room. Put it where the body is before announcing it.
Murder.afterAutopsy: The autopsy Truth Bullet has not been issued.
Murder.afterDirect: A direct murder — whoever was in the room saw it happen.
Murder.afterIndirect: A trap — nobody saw it, and setting it left traces of its own.
Murder.escapeIntro: {victim} and {third} walked out on {killer}. Nobody died, so there is no body to announce, no autopsy to issue and no Class Trial to hold. The incident simply ends.
Murder.escapeRoom: It happened in {room}, and what the fight left behind is still there.
Murder.escapeNoRoom: No room is recorded for this incident, so place whatever it left behind by hand.
Murder.escapeWitness: {victim} and {third} both saw who it was. What they do with that is the table's business.
Murder.escapeKiller: {killer} is not Blackened. Nothing has changed for them except that two people know.
Murder.actionBlocked: They have shut this one down for now.
Murder.actionHindered: They have made this harder — you roll at disadvantage.
Murder.noStressLeft: Resolution actions cost Sanity, and you have none.
Murder.killerChooses: Critical — the killer chooses: 2 Health, 2 Sanity, or 1 of each.

hinderedActions.one: {n} of their action at disadvantage for {turns} turns.
hinderedActions.other: {n} of their actions at disadvantage for {turns} turns.

blockedActions.one: {n} of their action shut down entirely for {turns} turns.
blockedActions.other: {n} of their actions shut down entirely for {turns} turns.

Murder.rolesSwapped: The roles are reversed. The killer is the one bleeding now.
Murder.victimDead: The victim is dead. The killer is Blackened.
Murder.resolutionNote: Stage 6. The killer now sees the Remnants on the map and can use resolution actions. Reinforced traces stay put. A crime tool that was used is destroyed.
Murder.thirdIntro: One free choice: get them out with you, take a side, or turn away.
Murder.actionSpent: You have already taken that one this incident.
Murder.drainStopped: The bleeding stops — no further Health or Sanity is lost this incident.
Murder.indirectBegins: The trap closes. The incident begins with the victim alone, losing 2 a turn.
Murder.tierZeroIntro: {actor} is swinging {item}, a Tier 0 object. A Tier 0 item may count as Tier 1 or 2 when the killer is being creative — how good is this use?
Murder.tierZeroNote: Tier 0 deals 1 damage, Tier 1 deals 2, Tier 2 deals 2 and 3 on a critical. Dismissing this leaves it at Tier 0.
Murder.improvised: Snatched a weapon out of the struggle: {item} (Tier {tier}).
Murder.improvisedNote: Grabbed mid-incident. A crime tool like any other.
Murder.cannotLeave: You are in an incident. The only way out is a crisis action.
Murder.actionsLocked: You are in an incident. Use your crisis actions; Hope Calls still work.
Murder.thirdJoined: {name} throws in with the killer and stays in the incident.
Murder.thirdLeft: {name} turns away and leaves. They take no part in this.
Murder.openingYours: This roll is yours, and it is the only one. It cannot be skipped.
Murder.openingRequired: This roll cannot be skipped. Throw it.
Murder.openingDeclined: {name} did not throw the opening roll. Stage 4 cannot be skipped: end this incident, or open it again from the panel.
Murder.openingRemnantNote: {name} sensed the attempt ({band}). Something of the struggle was left to notice.

leftRemnants.one: Leaves a trace behind, and the killer cannot wipe it.
leftRemnants.other: Leaves {n} traces behind, and the killer cannot wipe them.

Murder.keyRemnantsStale: The roles reversed, so the case changed: the five Key Remnants were planned around a killer who is now the victim. Plan a new set before the Investigation.
Murder.nightNoteDirect: It is night: the killer's opening roll has advantage.
Murder.nightNoteIndirect: It is night: the victim's opening roll has disadvantage.
Murder.betrayalNote: {third} walked in on this and is still standing. They may turn on {killer} now — the one killing in the game that needs no declaration in advance.
Murder.betrayalIntro: {third} kills {killer}. This closes as a second murder, with {third} as the killer and {killer} as the victim — a fresh incident from the opening roll, not a continuation of the one that just ended.
Murder.betrayalRule: Two bodies come out of this evening, and the Class Trial has two killings to untangle. Whoever is Blackened for the first is not automatically Blackened for the second.
Murder.betrayalAnnounce: A second incident opens on {killer} — the betrayal.
Murder.victimUnderAttack: Someone is moving on you. The incident has begun and the first turn is yours. Your crisis actions are on your character sheet, under Actions.
Murder.victimTrapSprung: The trap closes. You did not see it in time. The incident has begun and the first turn is yours — your crisis actions are on your character sheet, under Actions.
Murder.betrayTileHint: Kill the person you just helped. This opens a second incident with you as the killer and them as the victim, and leaves two bodies from one night. The GM confirms before anything happens.
Murder.criticalChoiceIntro: The blow lands exactly where you wanted it. Take both marks off the same place — their body, or their nerve.
Murder.ranOutTwoKillers: {victim} has nothing left. {killers} are both in this.
Murder.ranOutTwoKillersNote: End it now and the incident moves to the clean-up. Keep going and the turn order carries on — nobody loses a turn they were owed, and you can end it from the tracker whenever you like.
Murder.crowded: {name} walked in on top of {third}. Four people in one room is not a murder anybody can carry out — the incident is cancelled.
Murder.crowdedNote: Nobody dies. What the fight already did stands: the wounds, the Sanity, and anything it left on the floor.

Investigation.plannerIntro: Five clues for chapter {chapter}. Together they should narrow the suspects to {min}–{max} people.
Investigation.tokenGone: Its Remnant is gone from the map
Investigation.tooThin: Only {found} Key Remnants have been found. The minimum is {min} — below that the trial has no honest answer. Point the players at what is left, or let it stand and pay for it at the vote.
Investigation.createNote: Pick a room on any row not already on the map. Apply places that Key Remnant there: reinforced, tied to the crime, at the centre of the region. Rows already pointing at a token are left alone.

plannerCreated.one: Plan saved; {n} Key Remnant placed on the map.
plannerCreated.other: Plan saved; {n} Key Remnants placed on the map.

Investigation.keyLimitLine: {used} of {limit} used this chapter — the minimum is {min}.
Investigation.keyLimitOverride: Create more than the opening roll allows
Investigation.createHereIntro: They named a point of interest and you have decided there is something there. This puts it on the map, and can hang it on one of the five clues you planned.

Vault.stowTooltip: Put this in your stash (you must be in the room)
Vault.takeTooltip: Take this back out (you must be in the room)
Vault.notHere: You have to be standing in your own room to reach your stash.
Vault.noBullets: Truth Bullets are what you know, not things in a drawer.
Vault.overflowed: Your hands were full, so {item} went into your stash. Your {category} limit is unchanged.
Vault.foundInStash: Hidden in this room, you find {item}.
Vault.stole: You take {item} out of {who}'s hiding place. They will notice it is gone.
Vault.manageIntro: Everything a room is, one kind of fact per tab. Apply saves every tab at once, whichever one is showing.
Vault.manageNote: A favoured category gives advantage to anyone searching here for it — medicine in the medic's office. A bad one gives disadvantage — bandages in the boiler room — and a category can never be both. A room with no table of its own falls through to the global pool, so half-finished setup is fine.
Vault.bedroomsIntro: Whose bedroom each room is, and whether the stash in it has a built hiding place. One student, one bedroom.
Vault.doorsIntro: Which doors are locked right now, and which start a season locked. A season reset puts every door back to its start column.
Vault.searchIntro: What searching each room draws from, how many search tokens it has left, and what it is a sensible place to look for.
Vault.noRooms: This scene has no room regions yet.
Vault.noneSet: No bedrooms have been assigned yet.
Vault.twoRooms: {name} cannot have two bedrooms ({a} and {b}). Pick one.
Vault.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. Long tables, a serving hatch, and a smell of bleach nobody can place.
Vault.descriptionIntro: What each room looks like, in your own words. Anyone standing in a room can read its description by clicking the clock at the top of the screen.
Vault.descriptionNote: Plain text — it is shown to players exactly as typed. Leave one blank and the room simply has nothing written about it.
Vault.fogIntro: Which rooms each character has already discovered on this scene. The room they are standing in is always clear; this is only about rooms they have BEEN to, which show as a dim veil rather than full fog.
Vault.fogUncovered: {pct}% of this scene's surface belongs to no room region at all — it will show as permanent fog rather than a wall gap, which usually means a room still needs drawing.
Vault.fogNote: Discover all / Hide all replace every checkbox above for every character at once. The individual checkboxes are for one room, one character.
Vault.checkRooms: Check the rooms on this scene
Vault.checkIntro: The rooms themselves are data, and the glow around a doorway is only as good as they are. This looks for the faults that cannot be seen in the region editor: rooms that overlap, borders drawn away from the walls they describe, and openings too long to be a way out. It reports; it never edits your map.
Vault.checkClean: Nothing to report — the rooms on this scene are clean.
Vault.inspectNote: Take things out from Give / take items — a stashed item is an ordinary item on its owner's sheet.
Vault.rifleIntro: This is {who}'s stash, in {room}, and it is not hidden. Take one thing.
Vault.rifleNote: Free, and they will notice it is gone. A concealed stash needs a Search instead.
Vault.noOpenStashHere: There is no open stash in this room.
Vault.openStashNote: Not hidden. Anyone standing here can go through it.
Vault.keyDescription: Opens the door to {room}, which belongs to {owner}. Share a copy to let somebody else in.
Vault.keyShared: {who} gave you a copy of the key to {room}.
Vault.keyGave: {who} now has a copy of your key to {room}.
Vault.keyMissing: The door to {room} is locked. You do not have that key.
Vault.giveKeyNote: A copy — the owner keeps theirs. Only rooms that belong to somebody are listed: a room with no owner has no door to unlock.
Vault.noKeysToGive: No keys left to hand over — this character already holds one for every bedroom that has an owner.
Vault.lockedAtStartHint: Whether this door is locked when a season begins. A season reset puts every door back to this.

Chapter.keepItems: Keep their inventory (not a killing-game death)
Chapter.deathNote: Everything they carried is destroyed, Truth Bullets included. That cannot be undone. The body stays on the map, but the dead stop counting as being in the room: they cannot witness, be handed anything, or block a murder happening there.
Chapter.vaultPending: Their stash was emptied with them — the count above includes anything put away.
Chapter.stageSixTitle: That was the victim of the incident
Chapter.stageSixIntro: {victim} is the victim of the incident {killer} is in, and the incident is still running.
Chapter.stageSixWhat: Moving it to Stage 6 lets {killer} see the traces they left and spend Sanity trying to erase them. The incident stays open until you close it, so nothing is announced yet.
Chapter.revived: {name} is no longer marked dead. Their destroyed inventory does not come back.
Chapter.deadPanelNote: The dead take no actions and spend no Hope. You keep your sheet and your voice at the table. Brought back as a Monocub, this panel becomes Move and Confusion.
Chapter.deadCannotAct: {name} is dead and cannot take actions.
Chapter.noRooms: This scene has no room regions to gather anyone into.
Chapter.bodyNote: Calls everyone to the scene and switches the phase to Investigation. First it offers you the doubtful Prep traces, so you can say which belong to this murder.
Chapter.bodyFound: A body has been found in {room}.
Chapter.bodyCalled: Everyone is called to the scene. The Investigation begins.

bodyDone.one: {moved} moved to the scene, {promoted} trace made permanent.
bodyDone.other: {moved} moved to the scene, {promoted} traces made permanent.

Chapter.promoteTitle: Which traces belong to this murder?
Chapter.promoteIntro: These Prep traces were left while somebody gathered tools. Most mean nothing. Tick the ones that belong to this killing.
Chapter.promoteNote: Ticked traces stop being doubtful: they survive the chapter-end sweep and count as evidence tied to the crime. Leave the rest and they go with everything else.
Chapter.endIntro: Chapter {chapter} is wrapping up. Tick what should happen.
Chapter.optReveal: Reveal what every Truth Bullet really is ({n} still unidentified)
Chapter.optRemnants: Clear Faint Remnants from the map ({n} would go)
Chapter.optSweep: Sweep Truth Bullets for the new session ({n} removed, {kept} Faint kept)
Chapter.endNote: Reveal at the end of the chapter; sweep at the start of the next session. Usually two different evenings, which is why they are two ticks. The sweep and the Remnant clear are both permanent.

doneSweep.one: Truth Bullets swept away: {removed}. Faint ones carried over: {kept}.
doneSweep.other: Truth Bullets swept away: {removed}. Faint ones carried over: {kept}.

Chapter.sweepReminder: New session — remember the Truth Bullet sweep. Nothing has been deleted yet.
Chapter.moved: The clock now reads chapter {chapter}, session {session}.

typeless.one: 1 Truth Bullet has no real type recorded, so revealing cannot touch it. Set it from Give / take items.
typeless.other: {n} Truth Bullets have no real type recorded, so revealing cannot touch them. Set them from Give / take items.

Trial.presentTooltip: Present — put this on the table for everyone to see.
Trial.presentIntro: You are about to show {name} ({type}) to everyone. Only what you can see goes on the card. Never the GM's notes.
Trial.commentPlaceholder: e.g. This is why the timeline does not work.
Trial.presentNote: The debate is not open, so this simply goes on the table — nobody's turn to speak changes. Once the GM opens the debate, the same button becomes an OBJECTION.
Trial.notInTrial: Evidence is presented in a Class Trial. Outside one, share a copy instead.
Trial.failed: That could not be presented. Tell the GM.
Trial.logSummary: {total} presented this chapter, {objections} of them as an Objection.
Trial.logEmpty: Nothing has been presented this chapter yet.
Trial.objectionNobody: There is nobody else left to object to.
Trial.objectionWarning: An OBJECTION is not the same as showing evidence. It takes the debate: {objection} seconds in which only you may speak, then {rebuttal} seconds of rebuttal between you and the person you name. Showing evidence leaves the discussion running.
Trial.objectionNoFloor: The debate is not open, so there is nothing to interrupt. Show the evidence instead.
Trial.objectionDuringObjection: Somebody else's OBJECTION is running. Wait for their minute and the rebuttal that follows it.
Trial.objectionTooltip: OBJECTION — put this on the table and take the floor.
Trial.objectionNotYourRebuttal: This rebuttal is not yours. Only the two on the floor may object inside it.

Handover.shareTooltip: Share a copy with someone in this room
Handover.giveTooltip: Hand this to someone in this room
Handover.shareIntro: Who do you show {name} to? You are in {room}.
Handover.giveIntro: Who do you hand {name} to? You are in {room}.
Handover.shareNote: They get their own copy, you keep yours, and their copy is not bound by any failed analysis of yours. Costs no action.
Handover.giveNote: This leaves your inventory for good. Their carry limit still applies. No action.
Handover.nobodyHere: Nobody else in {room} to hand anything to.
Handover.tooFar: {name} is no longer in the room with you. Nothing changed hands.
Handover.theirHandsFull: {who} already carries the most {category} they can ({limit}).
Handover.failed: That handover did not go through. Tell the GM.
Handover.stuck: {who} handed over “{name}”, but their own copy could not be removed. Two exist now — delete one from their sheet.
Handover.alreadyHasIt: {who} already found that trace themselves. {name} would only be a duplicate.
Handover.receivedBulletFrom: {who} showed you {name}, and you have written down a copy.

Observe.anythingTitle: Observe — a question for the GM
Observe.requestPlaceholder: e.g. something to do with the body
Observe.requestPrompt: The dice are thrown. Now say what you were looking for. The GM matches it against the room without seeing your roll, so this makes nothing easier or harder.
Observe.requestSkipped: Nothing named — read as simply looking around.
Observe.sent: The GM is judging what you found.
Observe.noRuling: No GM settled what you were looking at. Your action is not spent.
Observe.failed: Nothing catches your eye. You take {stress} Sanity.
Observe.critIdentified: You found it, and you know what kind of trace it is.
Observe.whichRemnant: Which Remnant are they closest to?
Observe.pickNote: Traces tied to the crime first, then easiest to hardest. They have already rolled, and you are not shown the number — pick what actually matches what they asked for.
Observe.pickConfirm: That is what they are looking at
Observe.describeIntro: {actor} found something in {room}. Name it as they would, and say what they see.
Observe.critPrompt: Critical — the category is identified for them, and they have earned a substantial hint.
Observe.rerollLost: A Reroll arrived for an Observe with no record here. Score the new number against the same trace by hand, and take back the Truth Bullet if it no longer fits.
Observe.alreadyDescribed: This trace has been described before. The words below are what the last observer was told — change them only if the critical reveals something new.
Observe.generalHint: Take whatever is easiest to spot in this room. Settled by the dice.
Observe.nonObviousHint: Go for the hardest thing here instead. Settled by the dice.
Observe.followTracesHint: Retrace your own steps and find what you left behind. Settled by the dice.
Observe.specificHint: Say what you are looking for. The GM decides what your gaze lands on.
Observe.anythingHint: Something that is not a trace — a person, a machine, the weather. The GM rules on it.

TruthBullet.title: Truth Bullet
TruthBullet.name: Name — this is what the player sees
TruthBullet.shown: What the player is told it is
TruthBullet.shownAuto: By the rules — Key, Autopsy and Final arrive identified, the rest start Neutral
TruthBullet.shownReal: The real type — no analysis needed
TruthBullet.visibility: How hard the original was to spot
TruthBullet.visibilityTooltip: How visible the original Remnant was. This sets the difficulty of analysing it.
TruthBullet.faintField: Faint — survives the sweep at the start of the next session
TruthBullet.tiedField: Tied to the murder — floats to the top of the pack once identified
TruthBullet.faintTooltip: Doubtful connection to the case. Survives into the next session and can be analysed again.
TruthBullet.lockedTooltip: You failed to analyse this one this chapter. Try again next chapter — or hand a copy to somebody else, who is not bound by your failure.
TruthBullet.playerTextPlaceholder: What the person who found it actually sees.
TruthBullet.gmNote: Note for the GM (never shown to the player)
TruthBullet.gmNotePlaceholder: What it really means for the case.
TruthBullet.secretNote: The real type and your note stay on the GM side. They never reach the player's item.
TruthBullet.whereToFind: It is in your inventory, under Truth Bullets.
TruthBullet.reallyTooltip: GM only — what this Truth Bullet actually is.
TruthBullet.autopsyHint: The state of the body — the time it was discovered, and the cause of death. Handed out at the start of every Investigation, never rolled for. Everyone is ticked; untick the victim.
TruthBullet.autopsyTextPlaceholder: Time of discovery, cause of death, and anything else the body shows.
TruthBullet.autopsyNobody: Nobody is ticked, so there is nobody to give it to.

autopsyIssued.one: Autopsy Truth Bullet issued to {n} character.
autopsyIssued.other: Autopsy Truth Bullet issued to {n} characters.

TruthBullet.migratedTitle: Truth Bullets brought up to date

migrated.one: {n} Truth Bullet made before this version now carries a type, a visibility and a chapter. Its real type could not be recovered, so it is recorded as Neutral — correct it from Give / take items if it matters.
migrated.other: {n} Truth Bullets made before this version now carry a type, a visibility and a chapter. Their real type could not be recovered, so each is recorded as Neutral — correct the ones that matter from Give / take items.

imported.one: Merged {n} Truth Bullet record into the ledger.
imported.other: Merged {n} Truth Bullet records into the ledger.

TruthBullet.importFailed: That file is not a Truth Bullet ledger.

Inventory.overCap: {actor} is over the {category} limit ({held}/{limit}). Allowed — a GM granted it.
Inventory.full: You already carry the most {category} you can ({limit}).
Inventory.notCarried: (not picked up — that category is full)

Remnant.reinforced: That Remnant is reinforced and cannot be removed.

deathTied.one: The victim is dead: {n} trace from this chapter is now marked as tied to the murder. Untick the laundry in the Investigation Dashboard.
deathTied.other: The victim is dead: {n} traces from this chapter are now marked as tied to the murder. Untick the laundry in the Investigation Dashboard.

Remnant.noToken: {actor} has no token on any scene, so the trace could not be left. Tell the GM.
Remnant.noTokenGm: {actor} performed “{action}” with no token anywhere, so no Remnant was placed. Place one by hand if it matters.
Remnant.revealWarning: Remnants are your notes. Revealing this puts it on the map for everyone.
Remnant.searchNote: {actor} searched {room} for a {category} (rolled {total}) and came away with {item} — Tier {tier}.
Remnant.sabotageWorked: It worked: the project is frozen until {repair} is finished.
Remnant.sabotageFailed: It failed — the project is untouched, but the attempt left a trace.
Remnant.projectNote: {actor} worked on {project} in {room}, gaining {progress} progress, and rolled {total} to cover their tracks.
Remnant.cardPlayer: Something here is out of place. What it means is not obvious from looking — Observe the room to work it out.
Remnant.cardUnanalyzed: You have not worked out what this is yet. Analyze it to find out.
Remnant.cardEditNote: Saved when you leave the field, and copied onto the token and every Truth Bullet taken from this trace.
Remnant.cardSaveFailed: That did not save. See the console.

report.heading: Remnants
report.reinforcedNote: ★ = reinforced, and the killer cannot remove it.

Rest.alreadyThisTimeOfDay: You have already taken a {kind} this time of day.
Rest.alreadyThisSession: You have already taken a {kind} this session.
Rest.alreadyThisTimeOfDayShort: already taken this time of day
Rest.wrongRoom: No {kind} in {room}. Rooms that allow it: {rooms}
Rest.noRooms: No room on this map is marked for a {kind} yet. The GM sets that up per scene.
Rest.manageIntro: Mark which rooms allow a Short Rest and which allow a Long Rest. Per scene, so every season's map can differ.
Rest.noRegions: This scene has no room regions. Draw them on the Regions layer first.

Calls.noPool: This Monokuma has no Despair pool. Check the Despair bar.
Calls.nobodyHere: Nobody else is in this room.
Calls.noItems: Nobody carries anything that can be destroyed.
Calls.armed: {name} may now use {what} on their next roll.
Calls.sealed: {room} is sealed for this time of day.
Calls.effectFailed: {call} was paid for, but its effect could not be applied. See the console.
Calls.refunded: {call} did nothing, so the {cost} it cost has been returned.
Calls.silenced: {name} cannot spend Hope Calls until the clock moves.
Calls.silencedNotice: Monokuma has silenced you. No Hope Calls until this time of day ends.
Calls.chained: {name} is chained to {room} until the clock moves.
Calls.chainedNotice: Monokuma has chained you in place. You cannot leave this room until this time of day ends.
Calls.chainedBlocked: You are chained here until this time of day ends.
Calls.sealedBlocked: {room} is sealed for this time of day. Nobody gets in.
Calls.freeCritUsed: {name} takes the action and scores an automatic critical — no roll.
Calls.pendingTooltip: Waiting on your next roll: {what}. Spent the moment you roll.
Calls.noExperiences: This character has no experiences written down, so this Call has nothing to add.
Calls.armedTitle: A Call was made for you
Calls.armedForYou: Another student spent Hope on you: your next roll has {what}. It applies by itself.
Calls.newRulePrompt: Write the new rule. Every player sees it in chat, word for word.
Calls.newRulePlaceholder: e.g. From now on, nobody may enter the library alone.
Calls.newRuleNote: Twelve Despair buys a permanent change to the game. Make it count.
Calls.newRuleAnnounced: The new rule was announced to everyone.
Calls.noSuchRoom: There is no region called "{room}" on this scene.
Calls.progressRefused: {name} could not take the progress — it is already complete.
Calls.cannotAfford: You do not hold enough for this one.

Monokuma.marked: {name} is now a Monokuma: no actions, no Hope, Despair Calls instead, and free movement.
Monokuma.panelIntro: Tick the actors that are Monokumas, then say whose Despair pool each draws on. Without this, two Monokumas share the pool of whichever Gamemaster is looking at the sheet.
Monokuma.panelNote: A Monokuma has no actions and no Hope: their sheet shows Despair Calls instead. The pool decides which Gamemaster pays for them.
Monokuma.sharedPool: {name}'s pool is shared by: {actors}. Each Monokuma should have their own.

phase.eclipse: The lights are out. Everyone moves once, anywhere on the map, and nobody can see who went where. Nothing else happens until it ends — it is the game's one moment of total cover, and it is where a murder usually starts.
phase.dailyLife: Ordinary days inside the school. You have two actions each time of day to search rooms, work on projects, rest, talk, and prepare. Nobody has died yet this chapter — this is the part where you decide who you trust.
phase.investigation: A body has been found. The clock is still running, but what you do with it has changed: Observe traces on the map and Analyze what you collect, and every Truth Bullet you build is something you can present at the trial. What you fail to find, you will not have.
phase.classTrial: Everyone is in the room and one of you did it. Testimony, Objections, and finally the vote. Get it right and the killer is punished; get it wrong and everybody else is.

despair.title: What Despair is
despair.what: Despair is the GM side's currency. It fills when rolls at the table come up with Despair rather than Hope — which is to say, it is fed by your bad luck and your risks.
despair.spent: It is spent on Despair Calls: the moves that make life harder — pushing a scene, hardening a room, turning a screw. The more of it there is, the more the school can do to you.
despair.masked: How much is held is the GM's to see. The rows on screen show that it exists, not how much.
despair.noPools: No Monokuma has a pool yet.

status.actionsWhat: Two each time of day. Searching a room, working on a project, resting, observing a trace, analysing a Truth Bullet — each of those is one.
status.actionsWounded: With all your Health marked you get one instead of two, until somebody patches you up.
status.actionsNow: You have {left} of {max} left this time of day.
status.moveWhat: One move between rooms each time of day that costs you nothing. After that, changing rooms costs an action like anything else.
status.moveSpent: Your free Move is gone this time of day — moving now costs an action.
status.hopeWhat: Hope is yours, and it is spent on Hope Calls: helping somebody else's roll, leaning on an Experience, invoking your Ultimate, rerolling. It comes back when rolls go your way.

projects.title: What a project is
projects.what: A project is something that takes longer than one action: building it, fixing it, poisoning it, digging through it. Each one lives in a room and only moves when somebody works on it there.
projects.progress: Working on a project is an action, and a roll — how well it goes decides how much progress it takes. When the bar fills, the thing is done.
projects.secret: Some projects are private to the people working on them. If you cannot see one, it is not on your list.
